definition_en: to trick someone, to make them look silly, or to behave in a silly way
core_image: 愚人节里，同学指着同桌的鞋带说散了，其实没散
scene: 愚人节里，同学指着同桌的鞋带说散了，其实没散。Do not fool your friends with that trick.
sceneCN: 这里 fool 是「欺骗」（第 01 个义项）；句意是别用那个把戏骗朋友。

senses.title: To trick
senses.definition: to trick someone into believing something
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事
senses.example: Do not fool your friends with that trick.
senses.exampleCN: 别用那个把戏骗朋友。
senses.why: Fool comes from Latin follis, 'bellows, windbag'; a person who talks empty words was called a fool, and the verb came to mean tricking someone.
senses.whyCN: fool 源自拉丁语 follis「风箱、空袋子」；说空话的人被叫作傻瓜，动词便由此表示骗人。

senses.title: To make look silly
senses.definition: to make someone look silly
senses.definitionCN: 让人显得可笑
senses.example: The joke fooled everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个玩笑愚弄了屋里所有人。
senses.why: The verb widened from plain deception to making a person appear foolish, which is what a practical joke does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从单纯的欺骗扩展到让人显得愚蠢，恶作剧做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To behave silly
senses.definition: to behave in a silly way
senses.definitionCN: 行为不正经
senses.example: Stop fooling around and do your homework.
senses.exampleCN: 别胡闹了，做作业吧。
senses.why: The phrase fool around turns the word toward the subject's own silly behaviour instead of a trick played on someone.
senses.whyCN: fool around 这个说法把词义转向主语自己胡闹，而不是对别人设套。

definition_zh: 强迫；力量；武力；部队；影响力
definition_en: to make someone do something, physical strength, violence, a military group, or a strong influence
core_image: 一双手用力推开沉重的大门，门轴发出吱呀声
scene: 暴风迫使航班取消。The storm forced the flight to be cancelled.
sceneCN: 这里 force 是「强迫」（第 1 个义项）；句意：暴风迫使航班取消。

senses.title: To compel
senses.definition: to make someone do something they do not want to do
senses.definitionCN: 使某人做不想做的事
senses.example: The storm forced the flight to be cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风迫使航班取消。
senses.why: This is the main verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的动词义项。

senses.title: Strength
senses.definition: physical strength or energy
senses.definitionCN: 体力或能量
senses.example: The force of the wind bent the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 风力把树压弯了。
senses.why: The noun names the power behind the push.
senses.whyCN: 名词指推动背后的力量。

senses.title: Violence
senses.definition: the use of physical power against people
senses.definitionCN: 对人使用身体力量
senses.example: The police used force to stop the fight.
senses.exampleCN: 警察使用武力制止打斗。
senses.why: Strength applied against people becomes force.
senses.whyCN: 施加于人的力量成为武力。

senses.title: Military group
senses.definition: an organized group of soldiers or police
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的军人或警察队伍
senses.example: The armed forces arrived at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 武装部队在黎明时到达。
senses.why: An organized body of force is a force.
senses.whyCN: 有组织的武力团体也称为 force。

senses.title: Influence
senses.definition: a person or thing that strongly affects events
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响事件的人或事物
senses.example: She is a driving force in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是团队中的推动力。
senses.why: Power can be social rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 力量可以是社会性的而非物理的。

definition_en: to say what is likely to happen, especially about weather or business, or such a statement
core_image: 气象员站在大屏幕前，指着明天的云雨带讲解天气
scene: 天气预报说今晚有雨。The weather forecast says rain tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 forecast 是「预报」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天气预报说今晚有雨。

senses.title: Weather report
senses.definition: a statement about future weather
senses.definitionCN: 关于未来天气的说明
senses.example: The weather forecast says rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 天气预报说今晚有雨。
senses.why: This is the most familiar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最熟悉的义项。

senses.title: Business prediction
senses.definition: an estimate of future sales or results
senses.definitionCN: 对未来销售或结果的估计
senses.example: The sales forecast was too optimistic.
senses.exampleCN: 销售预测过于乐观。
senses.why: The weather model extends to money.
senses.whyCN: 天气模型延伸到金钱领域。

senses.title: To predict
senses.definition: to say what is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 说出可能发生的事
senses.example: Experts forecast slower growth.
senses.exampleCN: 专家预判增长会放缓。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of predicting.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为预测动作。

senses.title: A sign
senses.definition: something that shows what may come
senses.definitionCN: 显示未来可能发生之事的迹象
senses.example: Dark clouds are a forecast of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云是下雨的预兆。
senses.why: A forecast can be read from signs.
senses.whyCN: 预兆也可被当作预报来读。

definition_zh: 造林；植树成林；森林覆盖的建立
definition_en: the act or process of establishing forest cover by planting or sowing trees on land
core_image: 一片荒坡先被挖出整齐的树穴，随后苗木成片栽下，几年后连成绿色覆盖
scene: 荒坡上先挖出一排排树穴，随后苗木被成片栽下，几年后这里重新有了连续的林冠。 Rows of planting pits were dug on the bare slope, seedlings were set out in blocks, and within a few years continuous forest cover had returned: that whole effort is forestation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「建立森林覆盖的整个努力」（第 1 个义项：通过栽植建立森林）；句意为荒坡先挖穴、再成片栽苗，几年后恢复连续林冠，这一整套工作就是造林。

pos.zh: 新造林（在原本无林的土地上）

senses.title: Establishing forest cover
senses.definition: the act or process of establishing a forest on land by planting or sowing trees
senses.definitionCN: 通过栽植或播种在土地上建立森林的行为或过程
senses.example: Forestation began with a survey of the eroded slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 造林从对侵蚀坡地的调查开始。
senses.why: This is the umbrella sense: any deliberate creation of forest cover.
senses.whyCN: 这是总称义：任何有意建立森林覆盖的行为。

senses.title: Process over time
senses.titleCN: 随时间推进的造林过程
senses.definition: the multi-year process by which planted land develops into functioning forest
senses.definitionCN: 栽植土地在多年中发育为功能森林的过程
senses.example: Forestation is measured in decades, not seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 造林以十年计，而不是以季节计。
senses.why: The word can name the slow process rather than the single planting event.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名缓慢过程，而不是一次栽植事件。

senses.title: Afforestation on bare land
senses.definition: the creation of forest on land that has not recently carried forest
senses.definitionCN: 在近期没有森林的土地上建立森林
senses.example: Afforestation converted the old pasture into a new wood.
senses.exampleCN: 新造林把旧牧场变成一片新林地。
senses.why: Technical usage separates new forest on bare land from replanting after loss.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法把裸地上的新林与损失后的补植区分开。

senses.title: Reforestation after loss
senses.titleCN: 森林损失后的重新造林
senses.definition: the replanting of land that was formerly forested but has lost its tree cover
senses.definitionCN: 在曾经有林、后来失去树冠的土地上重新栽植
senses.example: Reforestation followed the fire that burned the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊被火烧过之后进行了重新造林。
senses.why: The same act is named by its history: the land remembers a previous forest.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作按土地历史命名：这块地记得从前的森林。

senses.title: Large-scale planting program
senses.definition: an organized program that plants many hectares or millions of seedlings
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地栽植许多公顷或数百万株苗木的计划
senses.example: The national forestation program planted a billion trees.
senses.exampleCN: 国家造林计划栽下了十亿棵树。
senses.why: Scale turns a practice into a policy instrument with targets and budgets.
senses.whyCN: 规模把实践变成有目标与预算的政策工具。

senses.title: Resulting forest area
senses.definition: the forest area that results from planting, considered as an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 栽植所产生的森林面积，作为结果来看
senses.example: The forestation now covers the whole western slope.
senses.exampleCN: 新造的林地现在覆盖整个西坡。
senses.why: The action noun also names its product: the area that now carries forest.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也命名产物：现在长着森林的那片面积。

senses.title: Carbon or climate forestation
senses.definition: forestation undertaken to absorb carbon or meet climate targets
senses.definitionCN: 为吸收碳或达成气候目标而进行的造林
senses.example: Carbon forestation is counted in tonnes of carbon dioxide stored.
senses.exampleCN: 碳汇造林以储存的二氧化碳吨数计量。
senses.why: The purpose changes the name: the forest is valued for stored carbon rather than timber.
senses.whyCN: 目的改变名称：这片森林的价值在储存的碳，而不在木材。

senses.title: Land-use conversion
senses.definition: the change of land use from agriculture or bare ground to forest
senses.definitionCN: 把农业用地或裸地改为林地
senses.example: Forestation changed the hydrology of the catchment within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 造林在十年内改变了这个集水区的水文状况。
senses.why: Seen from land-use planning, planting trees is a change of category, not only an act on a slope.
senses.whyCN: 从土地利用规划看，种树是类别改变，而不只是坡上的一项动作。

intro.en: Forestation is an English formation on forest plus the Latin-derived suffix -ation. Its technical branches, especially afforestation and reforestation, are nineteenth- and twentieth-century developments.
intro.cn: 该词由 forest 与拉丁来源后缀 -ation 构成；技术分支 afforestation、reforestation 在十九至二十世纪定型，具体年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base forest comes from Medieval Latin forestis through Old French. The suffix -ation comes from Latin -atio, which names an action or its result.
items.cn: 基础词 forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。后缀 -ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，命名动作或结果。

items.en: Forestation is recorded in nineteenth-century writing on land improvement. It was used alongside afforestation and reforestation, which became the more technical terms.
items.cn: forestation 见于十九世纪有关土地改良的写作。它与 afforestation、reforestation 并用，后两者后来成为更技术的术语。

items.en: Forestry separated afforestation, planting on land without recent forest, from reforestation, replanting after loss. Forestation remained the general cover term.
items.cn: 林业把 afforestation（在近期无林地上栽植）与 reforestation（损失后补植）分开；forestation 则保留为总称。

items.en: State tree-planting programs and soil-conservation schemes made forestation a policy word with targets, budgets and measured areas.
items.cn: 国家植树计划与水土保持方案使 forestation 成为带有目标、预算与测量面积的政策词。

items.en: Climate policy added carbon forestation, where the purpose is storage of carbon rather than timber or soil protection.
items.cn: 气候政策增加了碳汇造林，其目的不是木材或水土保护，而是碳储存。

note.en: The first group is close in sound or shares the base; the second group names the same act at different scales or from the opposite direction.
note.cn: 第一组读音接近或共享基础词；第二组在不同尺度或相反方向上命名同一行为。

entries.definition: the removal of forest cover; it is the reverse process, not a variant spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 毁林。除去森林覆盖，是相反过程，不是拼写变体。

entries.definition: planting a forest on land that has not recently been forested; it is a technical subtype of forestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在近期无林的土地上造林，是 forestation 的技术子类。

entries.definition: replanting land that was previously forested; it is another technical subtype.
entries.definitionCN: 重新造林。在曾经有林的土地上补植，是另一个技术子类。

entries.definition: the everyday act of planting trees; it does not require the result to become a forest.
entries.definitionCN: 植树。日常说法，不要求最终形成森林。

entries.definition: the restoration of plant cover of any kind, not necessarily trees.
entries.definitionCN: 植被恢复。恢复任何植物覆盖，不一定是树木。

entries.definition: the creation of new forest on bare or non-forest land; it is narrower than forestation.
entries.definitionCN: 新造林。在裸地或非林地上建立新林，比 forestation 窄。

entries.definition: the repair of a degraded forest's structure and function; it may involve natural regeneration, not only planting.
entries.definitionCN: 森林恢复。修复退化森林的结构与功能，可能依靠自然更新，而不只是栽植。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is forest and the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
normal.cn: 基础词是 forest，后缀 -ation 标记动作或结果。

normal.en: The technical pair is afforestation for new forest and reforestation for replanting.
normal.cn: 技术上的配对是：afforestation 指新造林，reforestation 指重新造林。

normal.en: Collocations: forestation program, forestation project, forestation rate.
normal.cn: 搭配：造林计划、造林项目、造林速度。

normal.en: Soil conservation and carbon policy are the two common policy frames.
normal.cn: 水土保持与碳政策是两种常见的政策框架。

normal.en: Forestation is the general word; tree planting is the everyday activity.
normal.cn: forestation 是总称；tree planting（植树）是日常活动。

abstract.en: Picture a bare slope marked out in rows before a single seedling goes in.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裸坡在栽下第一株苗之前就被划成一排排。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside turning from brown to green over ten annual photographs.
abstract.cn: 想象同一片山坡在十张年度照片里从褐色变成绿色。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where every hectare planted is entered as carbon stored.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每栽一公顷就记下一笔碳储存。

examples.en: The forestation project aimed to stabilise sand dunes along the coast.
examples.cn: 这个造林项目旨在稳住沿海沙丘。

examples.en: Forestation of the catchment reduced erosion within five years.
examples.cn: 集水区造林在五年内减少了侵蚀。

examples.en: Carbon forestation is only credited if the new forest survives.
examples.cn: 只有新林存活，碳汇造林才被计入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森林 + 行动」——把一片地变成森林的整套动作 → 造林

root: 由 forest 加拉丁来源后缀 -ation 构成；forest 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 forestis。afforestation 与 reforestation 在十九至二十世纪成为更细的技术术语；具体年代为大致估计。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act at different stages and scales: the umbrella act, the slow process, the two technical subtypes, the program, the resulting area, the climate purpose and the land-use change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一行为的不同阶段与尺度展开：总称行为、缓慢过程、两个技术子类、计划、结果面积、气候目的与土地用途改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare slope being turned into continuous green cover by deliberate planting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片裸坡通过有意栽植变成连续的绿色覆盖。

branches.en: ACT AND PROCESS: one deliberate act seen as an event and as a decade-long process.
branches.cn: 行为与过程：同一有意行为，既作事件看，也作十年过程看。

branches.en: TWO HISTORIES: new forest on bare land and replanting after loss.
branches.cn: 两种历史：裸地上的新林，与损失后的补植。

branches.en: SCALE AND RESULT: a program and the area it produces.
branches.cn: 规模与结果：计划以及它产生的面积。

branches.en: CLIMATE PURPOSE: the forest is planted to store carbon.
branches.cn: 气候目的：种林是为了储存碳。

branches.en: LAND-USE CHANGE: forest replaces another use and alters water and soil.
branches.cn: 土地用途改变：森林取代其他用途，并改变水土。

intro.en: Forestation is a transparent English formation: a borrowed base plus a Latin-derived action suffix, with technical subtypes added by prefixes.
intro.cn: forestation 是透明的英语构造：借入基础词加拉丁来源动作后缀，技术子类由前缀补充。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin forestis supplies forest; Latin -atio supplies -ation. The prefixes af- and re- create the two technical subtypes.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis 提供 forest；拉丁语 -atio 提供 -ation。前缀 af- 与 re- 造出两个技术子类。

definition_en: to stop being angry with someone, to pardon a wrong, to cancel a debt, or to ask politely
core_image: 紧握的拳头慢慢松开，怒气像沙子一样漏掉
scene: 她原谅了他的迟到。She forgave him for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 forgive 是「原谅」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她原谅了他的迟到。

senses.title: To stop being angry
senses.definition: to stop being angry with someone for a wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的过错而不再生气
senses.example: She forgave him for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她原谅了他的迟到。
senses.why: This is the everyday personal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的人际义项。

senses.title: To pardon
senses.definition: to pardon a serious wrong or crime
senses.definitionCN: 宽恕严重的过错或罪行
senses.example: The king forgave the prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 国王宽恕了那名囚犯。
senses.why: The word can carry the weight of law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以承载法律的重量。

senses.title: To cancel a debt
senses.definition: to officially cancel money that is owed
senses.definitionCN: 正式取消所欠的钱
senses.example: The bank forgave the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行免除了这笔贷款。
senses.why: A debt can be released like a grudge.
senses.whyCN: 债务可以像怨恨一样被释放。

senses.title: A polite opener
senses.definition: used politely before asking or interrupting
senses.definitionCN: 在提问或打断之前礼貌使用
senses.example: Forgive me, but I have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 请原谅，我有个问题。
senses.why: The pardon sense softens everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 宽恕义项让日常言语变得柔和。

definition_zh: 制定；构想；明确表述；按配方配制
definition_en: to express an idea precisely, or to work out a plan, rule or product in a fixed form
core_image: 散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序
scene: 团队把几周的讨论写成一份可执行的方案，交给上级审批。The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
sceneCN: 这里指把想法写成一份具体的行动方案（第 3 个义项：制定计划、政策或策略）；句意：团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。

senses.title: To express an idea precisely
senses.definition: to state an idea in clear, exact words so that it can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚准确的语言说出一个想法，使其可被检验
senses.example: He formulated the problem in one short sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一句短话把问题精确表述出来。
senses.why: A formula is a fixed form, and to formulate is to put thought into such a form.
senses.whyCN: 配方或公式是一种固定格式，而制定表述就是把思想放进这种格式。

senses.title: To write a formula in symbols
senses.definition: in chemistry or mathematics, to write a relation or a compound in standard symbols
senses.definitionCN: 在化学或数学中，用标准符号写出一个关系或一种化合物
senses.example: The students formulated the equation for the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们写出了这个反应的方程式。
senses.why: Symbols are the most exact kind of fixed form, so the word fits mathematics most literally.
senses.whyCN: 符号是最精确的固定格式，因此这个词在数学里最为字面。

senses.title: To devise a plan or policy
senses.definition: to work out a course of action in a form that others can follow
senses.definitionCN: 把一套行动安排成别人可以照着做的形式
senses.example: The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。
senses.why: A plan must be given a shape before it can be shared, and giving it shape is the work of this verb.
senses.whyCN: 计划必须先有形状才能被共享，而给它形状正是这个动词的工作。

senses.title: To state a theory precisely
senses.definition: to put a hypothesis into a form that can be tested and criticized
senses.definitionCN: 把假说放进一种可以被检验与批评的形式
senses.example: Newton formulated laws that still describe ordinary motion.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿提出了至今仍能描述日常运动的定律。
senses.why: A theory that stays vague cannot be tested, so formulating it is the first condition of science.
senses.whyCN: 含糊的理论无法检验，因此把它精确表述是科学的第一条件。

senses.title: To prepare a product to a formula
senses.definition: to mix a medicine, a food or a material according to a fixed recipe
senses.definitionCN: 按照固定配方混合药物、食品或材料
senses.example: The lab formulated the cream for sensitive skin.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为敏感肌肤配出了这款乳霜。
senses.why: Here the formula is a recipe rather than an equation, and the verb means to make the mixture.
senses.whyCN: 这里的配方是食谱而不是方程，动词意为把混合物做出来。

senses.title: To frame a question or argument
senses.titleCN: 把问题或论证组织成形
senses.definition: to arrange a question or an argument so that its parts are clear and ordered
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或论证安排得部分清楚、次序分明
senses.example: A good interviewer formulates the next question from the answer just given.
senses.exampleCN: 好的采访者会根据刚得到的回答组织下一个问题。
senses.why: Thinking becomes visible when it is given an order, and the verb names that ordering.
senses.whyCN: 思想在被赋予次序时才变得可见，这个动词命名的是那个安排次序的动作。

senses.title: To draw up rules or regulations
senses.definition: to set out rules in an official and precise wording
senses.definitionCN: 用正式而精确的措辞写出规则
senses.example: The committee formulated the rules for the new grant.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会拟订了这项新资助的规则。
senses.why: Rules must be fixed in words before they can bind anyone, which is a formal version of formulation.
senses.whyCN: 规则必须先固定成文字才能约束人，这是「成形」的正式版本。

senses.title: To compose a response or statement
senses.definition: to prepare a reply or a public statement in careful wording
senses.definitionCN: 用审慎的措辞准备一份答复或公开声明
senses.example: The office formulated a short response to the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对投诉拟定了一份简短回应。
senses.why: A response is an idea that must be given a public shape before it leaves the room.
senses.whyCN: 回应是一个必须先在室内成形、才能送出房间的想法。

intro.en: Formulate comes from the Latin noun for a small mould or a fixed pattern, and from a verb meaning to shape it. French passed the verb to English in the eighteenth century, and its senses spread from recipes to policies.
intro.cn: 本词出自拉丁语中表示小模子或固定格式的名词，以及一个意为按此成形的动词。法语在十八世纪把这个动词传给英语，含义从配方扩展到政策。

items.en: Forma meant shape, mould or pattern, and it stands behind the whole English family of form words.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指形状、模子或格式，英语中一整族与形式有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Formula was a small mould, and then a fixed wording or a set pattern.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词原指小模子，后来指固定的措辞或既定的格式。

items.en: The verb meant to shape something or to set it down in a fixed form.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为使成形，或按固定格式写下。

items.en: French carried the verb forward in the sense of putting an idea into exact words.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词推进到「把想法放进确切措辞」的意义。

items.en: English took it in the eighteenth century, when scientific and legal writing needed exact statements.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，当时科学与法律写作都需要精确陈述。

items.en: Chemistry kept the recipe sense, while policy and management took the planning sense.
items.cn: 化学保留了配方义，政策与管理则取用了制定计划之义。

note.en: The first group shares the shape root or its English family; the second group names nearby kinds of putting ideas into form. Formulate stresses giving an idea a precise and workable shape, while facilitate stresses removing obstacles so that work can proceed.
note.cn: 第一组共享形状词根或其英语词族；第二组是相邻的「使想法成形」方式。本词强调给想法一个精确可用的形状，便利类词强调搬走障碍让工作得以前进。

entries.definition: A fixed set of symbols, a recipe or a worn phrase.

entries.definition: The wording produced, and the act of producing it.

entries.definition: Made to a fixed pattern, often in a negative sense of stale wording.

entries.definition: The arrangement of a page or a file, from the same shape root.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的排列方式，出自同一形状词根。

entries.definition: To invent or work out a plan; the emphasis is on invention, not exact wording.
entries.definitionCN: 发明或想出计划；强调发明，而非精确措辞。

entries.definition: To put a question or a statement into words; it stresses the frame around it.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题或陈述组织成话；强调外围框架。

entries.definition: To write a first version; it need not be precise yet.
entries.definitionCN: 写出初稿；此时还不必精确。

entries.definition: To express clearly in speech; it stresses clear delivery rather than planned form.
entries.definitionCN: 口头清楚表达；强调表达清楚，而非计划好的形式。

entries.definition: To put parts together into a whole, as in writing or music.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分组合成整体，如写作或音乐。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the shape root, the real family and the objects that show planning, science and recipes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用形状词根、真实同族词，以及能显示计划、科学与配方的宾语。

normal.en: The root means shape, and a small mould is inside the noun, so the verb means to give an idea a mould.
normal.cn: 词根意为形状，名词里含有一个小模子，因此动词意为给想法一个模子。

normal.en: The family runs formula, formulation, formulaic and formulator.
normal.cn: 同族词有公式、表述、公式化的与制定者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: formulate a plan, formulate a policy, formulate a theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：制定计划、制定政策、提出理论。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the literal recipe sense, and politics keeps the planning sense.
normal.cn: 化学保留字面的配方义，政治保留制定计划的义项。

normal.en: A statement that cannot be put into exact words has not yet been formulated.
normal.cn: 还不能被放进确切措辞的陈述，就还没有被制定成形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all give an idea a fixed shape: exact words, symbols, a plan, a theory, a recipe, a question, a rule and a public reply.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose notes on a table copied into a numbered recipe card, every line with a fixed amount and a fixed order.
core.cn: 核心意象：散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: an idea put into exact words, and a question or an argument ordered.
branches.cn: 陈述：被放进准确措辞的想法，以及被安排好次序的问题或论证。

branches.en: THE SYMBOLS AND THE THEORY: an equation written, and a hypothesis made testable.
branches.cn: 符号与理论：写出的方程，以及变得可检验的假说。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a course of action shaped so that others can follow it.
branches.cn: 计划：成形后别人可以照着走的行动安排。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: a medicine, food or material mixed to a fixed formula.
branches.cn: 配方：按固定配方混合的药物、食品或材料。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL WORD: rules drawn up, and a reply carefully worded.
branches.cn: 正式文字：拟订的规则与措辞审慎的答复。

definition_en: the act of expressing an idea precisely, or the particular mixture and wording that results
core_image: 一张纸上先写出一句精确的话，旁边再排出配比表
scene: 这里指「表述」。 The formulation of the policy took months of drafting and redrafting.
sceneCN: 这里 formulation 是「制定、表述」（第 1 个义项：把想法整理成明确文字）；句意：这项政策的制定花了几个月反复起草。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、修改批注、会议桌、印章。

senses.title: Putting an idea into exact words
senses.titleCN: 表述：把想法压成一句准话
senses.definition: the act of expressing a thought or plan in clear, precise language
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚、精确的语言表达思想或计划的行为
senses.example: The formulation of the question decided what could count as an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 问题的表述方式决定了什么才算答案。
senses.why: formula is a small form. Formulation gives an idea a definite shape in words, the way a mold gives metal a shape.
senses.whyCN: formula 是“小形式”。formulation 用文字给想法一个确定形状，就像模具给金属一个形状。

senses.title: Drafting a policy
senses.titleCN: 制定：把政策一条条写出来
senses.definition: the process of designing and writing a policy, strategy or plan
senses.definitionCN: 设计并写出政策、战略或计划的过程
senses.example: The formulation of the new tax rules involved three ministries.
senses.exampleCN: 新税则的制定涉及三个部委。
senses.why: Policy does not exist until it is written down. Formulation is the moment an intention acquires clauses, numbers and a signature line.
senses.whyCN: 政策在写下来之前并不存在。formulation 就是意图获得条款、数字与签字栏的那一刻。

senses.title: A chemical recipe
senses.definition: a specific mixture of ingredients and their proportions, especially in medicine or industry
senses.definitionCN: 成分及其比例的特定混合，尤用于医药或工业
senses.example: The new formulation dissolves faster and tastes less bitter.
senses.exampleCN: 新配方溶解更快，苦味也更少。
senses.why: This is the most concrete sense: the formula is a list of quantities. The word names both the list and the resulting product.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的义项：formula 是一张数量清单。这个词既命名清单，也命名产物。

senses.title: Stating it as a formula
senses.titleCN: 公式表达：把关系写成符号
senses.definition: the expression of a relationship in mathematical symbols
senses.definitionCN: 用数学符号表达某种关系
senses.example: The formulation of the model uses two variables and one constant.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型的公式表达使用两个变量和一个常数。
senses.why: Mathematics strips the idea to symbols. The same 'give it a form' act now produces an equation rather than a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 数学把想法剥到符号层。同一个“给它一个形式”的动作，现在产出的是方程而不是句子。

senses.title: Building a theory
senses.titleCN: 理论建构：把假设搭成体系
senses.definition: the construction of a theory or hypothesis in a defined and testable form
senses.definitionCN: 以明确且可检验的形式构建理论或假设
senses.example: Her formulation of the problem avoided the usual assumption of perfect information.
senses.exampleCN: 她对问题的理论建构避开了常见的完全信息假设。
senses.why: A theory is formulation all the way down: assumptions, definitions and predictions are all given form before anything can be tested.
senses.whyCN: 理论从头到尾都是 formulation：假设、定义与预测都必须先获得形式，才谈得上检验。

senses.title: The finished product form
senses.titleCN: 剂型：做成药片还是液体
senses.definition: the physical form in which a medicine or product is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 药品或产品供应的物理形态
senses.example: The same drug is sold in tablet and liquid formulations.
senses.exampleCN: 同一种药有片剂和液剂两种剂型。
senses.why: Here formulation means the shape the product finally takes. The active ingredient is the same; the form is the difference.
senses.whyCN: 这里 formulation 指产品最终采取的形状。有效成分相同，差别在形式。

senses.title: Setting out a problem
senses.titleCN: 问题形式化：先把题目写清楚
senses.definition: the formal statement of a problem so that it can be solved or computed
senses.definitionCN: 为使问题可解或可计算而作的正式陈述
senses.example: A good formulation often makes the solution obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的问题表述常让解法变得显然。
senses.why: This sense treats formulation as half the solution. Once the problem is stated in the right variables, the hard part is already done.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把 formulation 当作解法的一半。一旦用正确的变量表述问题，难的部分已经完成。

senses.title: A statement repeated as a formula
senses.definition: a fixed phrase used repeatedly, often losing its original force
senses.definitionCN: 被反复使用、常失去原有力量的固定说法
senses.example: The minister's formulation about 'shared responsibility' satisfied nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 部长那句关于“共同责任”的套话谁也没说服。
senses.why: A formulation can harden into a formula. What was once a precise shaping becomes a ready-made block dropped into any speech.
senses.whyCN: formulation 会硬化成 formula。曾经精确的塑形，变成可以塞进任何演讲的现成积木。

intro.en: Formulation comes from formulate, from Latin formulare 'to form', built on formula, a diminutive of forma 'form, shape'. The word is about giving something a definite shape.
intro.cn: formulation 来自 formulate，而 formulate 出自拉丁 formulare“成形”，建立在 formula 之上，而 formula 是 forma“形式、形状”的指小形式。这个词讲的是给某物一个确定形状。

items.en: forma meant 'form, shape, mold'. It also meant 'beauty', because a well-shaped thing was thought beautiful; English form and formal descend from it.
items.cn: forma 意为“形式、形状、模具”。它也表示“美”，因为形状好的东西被认为美；英语 form、formal 由此而来。

items.en: formula was a small forma, 'a little shape'. In law it meant a fixed form of words, which is how the modern 'formula' sense began.
items.cn: formula 是“小形式”，即一个小 shape。在法律中它指固定的措辞格式，现代“公式”义正由此开始。

items.en: formulare 'to shape, to express in a fixed form' turns the noun into a verb. The verb covers both drafting a text and mixing a preparation.
items.cn: formulare“塑形、以固定形式表达”把名词变成动词。这个动词既涵盖起草文本，也涵盖配制混合物。

items.en: English formulate appears in the 19th century. It inherits both the verbal sense, to state precisely, and the chemical sense, to prepare by recipe.
items.cn: 英语 formulate 于 19 世纪出现。它继承了两种含义：精确陈述的言语义，以及按配方配制的化学义。

items.en: Formulation adds -ation, from Latin -atio, naming the process or its result. The noun is common in policy, pharmacy and mathematics.
items.cn: formulation 加 -ation（来自拉丁 -atio），命名过程或结果。这个名词常见于政策、药学与数学。

items.en: In the 20th century formulation becomes standard in policy and strategy writing, where it names the drafting stage before adoption.
items.cn: 20 世纪 formulation 成为政策与战略写作的标准词，命名通过之前的起草阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the form- root but each adds a different suffix; the near-meaning group all involve putting something into a definite shape, verbal or material.
note.cn: 形近组共享 form- 词根，但各加不同后缀；近义组都涉及把某物放进确定形状，或言语或物质。

entries.definition: a fixed expression, recipe or equation. It is the shaped thing; formulation is the shaping act.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的说法、配方或公式。它是被塑成之物；formulation 是塑形行为。

entries.definition: to express precisely or to prepare by recipe. It is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 确切表达；按配方配制。它是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: the process of coming into being, as of a structure or group. It uses formare 'to form' directly, without the -ula diminutive.
entries.definitionCN: 形成、构成的过程，如结构或群体的形成。它直接用 formare“形成”，没有 -ula 指小成分。

entries.definition: the act of putting a thought into words. It is broader than formulation and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法放进文字的行为。它比 formulation 更宽泛，也更不技术化。

entries.definition: the particular words used to say something. It focuses on the verbal surface, not the underlying design.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表达某事的特定措辞。它聚焦言语表面，而非底层设计。

entries.definition: the act of combining parts into a whole, as in music or writing. It is broader and often artistic.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分合成整体，如音乐或写作。它更宽泛，常带艺术性。

entries.definition: the act of making something ready, especially a mixture. It covers the pharmacy sense but not the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物准备好的行为，尤指配制混合物。它覆盖药学义，但不含政策义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: forma 'shape' + -ula 'little': a formula is a little shape, and formulation is giving an idea that shape.
normal.cn: forma“形状”+ -ula“小”：formula 是一个小形状，formulation 就是给想法这个形状。

normal.en: policy formulation and strategy formulation are the two standard policy collocations.
normal.cn: policy formulation 与 strategy formulation 是两个标准政策搭配。

normal.en: drug formulation is the pharmacy sense: same active ingredient, different physical form.
normal.cn: drug formulation 是药学义：同一有效成分，不同物理形态。

normal.en: A good mathematical formulation often solves half the problem before calculation starts.
normal.cn: 好的数学表述常在计算开始前就解决了一半问题。

normal.en: Note the pair formula and formulation: one is the fixed shape, the other the act of shaping.
normal.cn: 注意 formula 与 formulation 这一对：一个是固定形状，一个是塑形动作。

abstract.en: Think of clay pressed into a mold and lifted out with a clean edge.
abstract.cn: 想象黏土压进模具，取出时边缘干净。

abstract.en: Think of a long argument reduced to one sentence on an index card.
abstract.cn: 想象一段长论证被压缩成卡片上的一句话。

abstract.en: Think of a cook writing exact grams beside each ingredient, then handing the card to a factory.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师在每种配料旁写下精确克数，然后把卡片交给工厂。

examples.en: The formulation of the hypothesis took longer than the experiment itself.
examples.cn: 假设的表述比实验本身花的时间还长。

examples.en: The company changed the formulation to remove the artificial colour.
examples.cn: 公司修改配方，去掉了人工色素。

examples.en: Clear formulation is a courtesy to the reader.
examples.cn: 清晰的表述是对读者的礼貌。

dict_mnemonic.text: “form（形式）+ ulate”——给想法一个形式，再写出来 → formulation 表述、配方

root: 拉丁 forma“形式、形状” → formula（forma 的指小形式，固定措辞/配方）→ formulare“塑形、表述” → formulate + -ation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one act: an idea or a substance is given a definite form, so that it can be repeated, tested or manufactured.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：想法或物质被赋予确定形式，从而可以被重复、检验或制造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clay pressed into a mold.
core.cn: 核心意象：黏土被压进模具。

branches.en: WORDS: a precise statement and a hardened stock phrase are the same shaping, one still alive and one gone rigid.
branches.cn: 文字：精确表述与僵硬套话是同一种塑形，一个还活着，一个已硬化。

branches.en: POLICY: the drafting stage gives an intention clauses and numbers before adoption.
branches.cn: 政策：起草阶段在通过之前给意图配上条款与数字。

branches.en: MATTER: a recipe and a finished dosage form are the list and the resulting shape of the same mixture.
branches.cn: 物质：配方与最终剂型，是同一混合物的清单与成品形状。

branches.en: SYMBOLS: mathematical statement and formal problem setting reduce the idea to variables and constraints.
branches.cn: 符号：数学表述与问题形式化，把想法压缩成变量与约束。

branches.en: THEORY: assumptions, definitions and predictions are all given form before testing begins.
branches.cn: 理论：假设、定义与预测在检验开始前都必须获得形式。

intro.en: Formulation is formulate plus -ation. The form- stem means 'shape', -ula is a diminutive, -ate makes a verb and -ation names the process.
intro.cn: formulation 是 formulate 加 -ation。form- 词干意为“形状”，-ula 是指小成分，-ate 构成动词，-ation 命名过程。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from forma 'shape' to formula 'little shape, fixed wording' to formulare 'shape, express'. English relatives include form, formal, format and formulate.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 forma“形状”到 formula“小形状、固定措辞”再到 formulare“塑形、表达”。英语同族词包括 form、formal、format、formulate。

items.meaning: to state precisely; to prepare by recipe
items.meaningCN: 确切表述；按配方配制（-ate 动词后缀）
items.example: The team formulated a clear hypothesis.
items.exampleCN: 团队提出了一个清晰的假设。

items.meaning: the act or result of shaping
items.meaningCN: 表述；制定；配方（-ation 过程名词）
items.exampleCN: 这份表述被修改了两次。

items.meaning: a fixed phrase, recipe or equation
items.meaningCN: 公式；配方（forma 的指小形式）

items.meaning: the shape or structure of something
items.meaningCN: 形式；形状（同一词根的基础名词）
items.example: Water takes the form of the container.

items.meaning: following an established shape or rule
items.meaningCN: 正式的；形式上的（-alis 关系形容词）
items.example: The letter was too formal for a friend.
items.exampleCN: 这封信对朋友来说太正式了。

items.meaning: the arrangement or layout of something
items.meaningCN: 格式；版式（-atus 事物名词）
items.example: The file format is not supported.

items.meaning: a book of approved formulas or medicines
items.meaningCN: 处方集；公式集（-ary 集合名词）
items.example: The hospital formulary lists two hundred drugs.
items.exampleCN: 医院处方集列出两百种药。

items.meaning: to state or prepare again in a new form
items.meaningCN: 重新表述；重新配制（re-“再次”）
items.example: They reformulated the question to avoid ambiguity.
items.exampleCN: 他们重新表述问题以避免歧义。

definition_zh: 向前；向外；出来；从某时起
definition_en: forward, outward, out from a place, or onward from a point in time
core_image: 门被推开，一个人从屋里走到阳光下
scene: 他走上前去说明情况。He came forth to explain.
sceneCN: 这里 forth 是「向前」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他走上前去说明情况。

senses.title: Forward
senses.definition: forward in space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上向前
senses.example: He came forth to explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他走上前去说明情况。
senses.why: This is the core directional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的方向义项。

senses.title: Outward
senses.definition: out from a place or into view
senses.definitionCN: 从某处出来或进入视线
senses.example: The sun broke forth from the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从云层中透出来。
senses.why: Light and sound also move outward.
senses.whyCN: 光和声音也会向外传播。

senses.title: Into being
senses.definition: used with verbs to mean producing or appearing
senses.definitionCN: 与动词连用表示产生或出现
senses.example: The tree brought forth new leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这棵树长出新叶。
senses.why: A thing can come forth into existence.
senses.whyCN: 事物可以产生出来。

senses.title: Onward in time
senses.definition: onward from a point in time
senses.definitionCN: 从某个时间点往后
senses.example: From that day forth, he walked to work.
senses.exampleCN: 从那天起，他步行上班。
senses.why: Space and time share the same direction.
senses.whyCN: 空间与时间共享同一个方向。

intro.en: Forth is an old Germanic word for forward.
intro.cn: forth 是一个表示向前的古老日耳曼语词。

items.en: Forth meant forward or onward.
items.cn: forth 意为向前或继续向前。

items.en: It was used with verbs of moving and bringing.
items.cn: 它常与移动和带来的动词连用。

items.en: Set forth came to mean to explain.
items.cn: set forth 逐渐表示阐述。

items.en: Back and forth described repeated movement.
items.cn: back and forth 描述反复移动。

items.en: The word became rare alone but lives in phrases.
items.cn: 这个词单独使用变少，却活在短语里。

note.en: Forth is compared with similar-looking words and with words for direction.
note.cn: 把 forth 与形近词以及表示方向的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Forth is the door opening toward the outside world.
normalIntro.cn: forth 是一扇朝外部世界打开的门。

normal.en: He came forth to explain.
normal.cn: 他走上前去说明情况。

normal.en: The sun broke forth from the clouds.

normal.cn: 从那天起，他步行上班。

normal.en: She paced back and forth.
normal.cn: 她来回踱步。

abstract.en: Forth is motion that refuses to stay hidden.
abstract.cn: forth 是不肯继续隐藏的运动。

abstract.en: Words set forth become shared.
abstract.cn: 被阐述出来的话就变成共有的。

abstract.en: Time also moves forth, one day at a time.
abstract.cn: 时间也一天一天地向前走。

examples.en: He came forth to explain.

dict_mnemonic.text: forth 和 forward 是亲戚：都表示向前、向外，只是 forth 更古老，也更常躲在短语里。

root: 源自古英语 forth（向前），核心义「朝外、朝前离开原位」。

sensesIntro.en: Forth means forward, outward, into being, or onward in time.
sensesIntro.cn: forth 意为向前、向外、出来或从某时起。

core.en: Movement away from a starting point.
core.cn: 离开起点的运动。

branches.en: A person steps forward.
branches.cn: 一个人向前迈步。

branches.en: Light leaves the clouds.
branches.cn: 光离开云层。

branches.en: Leaves come into being.
branches.cn: 叶子生长出来。

branches.en: A routine begins and continues.
branches.cn: 一种习惯开始并继续。

branches.en: Space and time both move outward.
branches.cn: 空间与时间都向外延伸。

intro.en: Forth gathers a family of forward and immediate words.
intro.cn: forth 聚拢了表示向前与立即的词族。

latinIntro.en: Forth is Germanic; Latin porro, forward, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: forth 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 porro（向前）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 即将出版的那本书很短。

items.meaning: moving one way and then the other
items.example: The boat rocked back and forth.
Bring pens, paper, and so forth.
The rules are set forth below.
The plan brought forth new ideas.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划产生了新想法。

definition_en: strength of mind that lets a person endure pain or hardship calmly
core_image: 一个人拄着拐杖走过长长的雪地，每一步都很慢，却一步也没有停
scene: 手术后的第三周，他每天沿走廊走二十步，从不让人扶。The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
sceneCN: 这里 fortitude 指忍痛坚持的坚毅（第 1 个义项：在痛苦中保持的力量）；句意为护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

senses.title: Courage in pain
senses.definition: the strength to bear physical pain without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 承受身体痛苦而不垮掉的力量
senses.example: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。
senses.why: This sense is about holding still under pain, not about fighting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是在痛苦下稳住，而不是与痛苦搏斗。

senses.title: Courage over years
senses.definition: the courage that lasts through long hardship rather than one crisis
senses.definitionCN: 穿过漫长困苦、而非一次危机的勇气
senses.example: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 她以不曾中断的坚毅独自养大三个孩子。
senses.why: A single hard hour needs nerve; a decade needs fortitude.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的一小时需要胆量；十年需要坚毅。

senses.title: Moral strength
senses.definition: the strength to keep to one's principles under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下守住原则的力量
senses.example: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他以沉静的刚毅拒绝了贿赂。
senses.why: Here the pain is not bodily but social: the cost is being disliked.
senses.whyCN: 这里的痛苦不是身体的，而是社会的：代价是被讨厌。

senses.title: Calm endurance
senses.definition: endurance without drama or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 不带戏剧性、也不抱怨的忍耐
senses.example: Her fortitude showed in what she never said.
senses.exampleCN: 她的坚忍体现在她从不说的那些话里。
senses.why: Endurance without complaint is the form strength takes when no one is watching.
senses.whyCN: 无人注视时，力量就表现为不抱怨的忍耐。

senses.title: Courage without display
senses.definition: strength that does not need to be seen to exist
senses.definitionCN: 无需被看见也存在的力量
senses.example: There was no speech, only fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 没有演说，只有坚毅。
senses.why: The word prefers the quiet form: it describes a state, not a performance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词偏爱安静的形式：它描述状态，而非表演。

senses.title: Fortitude in adversity
senses.definition: the quality that keeps a person upright when circumstances turn bad
senses.definitionCN: 境况转坏时使人不倒的品质
senses.example: The town met the flood with stubborn fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇以倔强的坚毅面对洪水。
senses.why: Bad circumstances are the test that turns a capacity into a habit.
senses.whyCN: 恶劣境况是把能力变成习惯的检验。

senses.title: Fortitude of belief
senses.definition: the strength to hold a faith or conviction against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 在反对中守住信仰或信念的力量
senses.example: The small congregation kept its fortitude through years of pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小教会在多年压力中保持坚贞。
senses.why: Faith under pressure is held by the same muscle that holds a body upright.
senses.whyCN: 压力下的信念，由撑住身体的同一块肌肉撑着。

senses.title: Physical stamina
senses.definition: the bodily strength to keep going when tired
senses.definitionCN: 疲倦时仍能继续的身体力量
senses.example: Long marches test fortitude more than courage.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军考验的更多是耐久，而不是勇气。
senses.why: The word can lean toward the body, though its usual home is the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以偏向身体，尽管它通常住在心智里。

intro.en: Fortitude comes from a Latin word for strength, and it is strength thought of as a thing a person can hold.
intro.cn: fortitude 来自一个意为「力量」的拉丁词，它是被当作人所能持有之物来想的力量。

items.en: English took the noun in the 12c. through French, first as a general word for strength.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪经法语借入这个名词，最初泛指力量。

items.en: Fortitudo meant 'strength, courage', and was one of the four classical virtues.
items.cn: fortitudo 意为「力量、勇气」，是四种古典美德之一。

items.en: Fortis means strong, brave, and gives fortify and fortress.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、勇敢，给出 fortify 与 fortress。

items.en: Medieval writers ranked fortitude as the virtue that holds the other virtues steady under attack.
items.cn: 中世纪作者把坚毅列为在攻击下稳住其它美德的美德。

items.en: Modern English narrowed it to quiet endurance, especially under pain or long hardship.
items.cn: 现代英语把它收窄为安静的忍耐，尤其在痛苦或长期困苦之下。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the strong root; the near-meaning group separates kinds of courage.
note.cn: 形近组共享「强」的词根；近义组区分不同种类的勇气。

entries.definition: to make stronger or better defended.
a defensive work or the act of strengthening.
a heavily defended stronghold.
showing quiet strength.
the ability to recover after difficulty.
the power to keep going through fatigue.
firm determination to do something.
enduring pain or loss without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 不抱怨地忍受痛苦或损失。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of slow steps across a long field of snow.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「在长长的雪地里一步一步慢慢走」的画面。

normal.en: Fortitude contains fort: a fort stands because it is built to take hits.
normal.cn: fortitude 里有 fort（堡垒）：堡垒能立住，是因为它造来承受打击。

normal.en: Link with fortify and fortress: one makes strong, one is strong.
normal.cn: 和 fortify、fortress 联系：一个加固，一个坚固。

normal.en: Think of a long walk rather than a single leap.
normal.cn: 想象一段长走，而不是一次跳跃。

normal.en: Say FOR-ti-tood; the heavy first syllable sounds like a planted foot.
normal.cn: 读成 FOR-ti-tood，沉甸甸的第一个音节像一只踏稳的脚。

normal.en: Shop it with patience: patience waits, fortitude holds.
normal.cn: 和 patience 一起记：patience 是等，fortitude 是撑住。

abstract.en: Courage meets a moment; fortitude meets a season.
abstract.cn: 勇气面对一个时刻，坚毅面对一个季节。

abstract.en: The strongest thing in a room is often the person saying nothing.
abstract.cn: 屋里最强的，常常是一言不发的那个人。

abstract.en: Strength held quietly does not need an audience to be real.
abstract.cn: 安静持有的力量，不需要观众才算真实。

examples.en: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
examples.cn: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

examples.en: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.

examples.en: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.

dict_mnemonic.text: fort（强）+ itude（名词）：一直强着的状态，就是「坚毅」。

root: 拉丁语 fortis（强、勇）→ fortitudo（力量、勇气）

sensesIntro.en: Fortitude is strength that holds rather than strikes; the senses differ in what is being held against, pain, time, pressure or fatigue.
sensesIntro.cn: fortitude 是「撑住」而非「出击」的力量；各义项的差别在于所抵抗的是痛苦、时间、压力，还是疲惫。

core.en: STRENGTH THAT HOLDS
core.cn: 撑住的力量

branches.en: Pain and its quiet bearing.
branches.cn: 痛苦与对其安静的承受。

branches.en: Long hardship and bad circumstances.
branches.cn: 长期困苦与恶劣境况。

branches.en: Principles and faith held under pressure.
branches.cn: 压力下守住的准则与信念。

branches.en: The unshown form: strength without performance.
branches.cn: 不展示的形态：没有表演的力量。

branches.en: The bodily version, stamina under fatigue.
branches.cn: 身体版本：疲惫中的耐久。

intro.en: The fort family is about making and being strong: fortify strengthens, fortress defends, fortitude endures.
intro.cn: fort 词族与「使强」和「强」有关：fortify 加固，fortress 防御，fortitude 忍耐。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis is the adjective strong; fortitudo turns it into a quality a person can possess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 是形容词「强」；fortitudo 把它变成一种人可以拥有的品质。

items.meaning: a making strong, or the work built

items.example: The fortress held for a month.
The force of the wave broke the door.

definition_zh: 两星期；十四天；两周假期
definition_en: a period of two weeks, or a two-week break
core_image: 日历上十四个格子被一条线连在一起
scene: 我们两周后见面。We will meet in a fortnight.
sceneCN: 这里 fortnight 是「两星期」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们两周后见面。

senses.title: Two weeks
senses.definition: a period of fourteen days
senses.definitionCN: 十四天的一段时间
senses.example: We will meet in a fortnight.
senses.exampleCN: 我们两周后见面。
senses.why: This is the basic British time sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的英式时间义项。

senses.title: Every two weeks
senses.definition: used for events that happen every two weeks
senses.definitionCN: 用于每两周发生一次的事
senses.example: The club meets every fortnight.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部每两周聚会一次。
senses.why: A length of time becomes a rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间变成一种节奏。

senses.title: A two-week break
senses.definition: a holiday lasting two weeks
senses.definitionCN: 持续两周的假期
senses.example: They took a fortnight's holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们休了两周假。
senses.why: British speech measures holidays in fortnights.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语用两星期来衡量假期。

intro.en: Fortnight is a contraction of fourteen nights.
intro.cn: fortnight 是 fourteen nights（十四个夜晚）的缩合。

items.en: Feowertyne niht meant fourteen nights.
items.cn: feowertyne niht 意为十四个夜晚。

items.en: The phrase shrank to fourtenight.
items.cn: 这个短语缩略为 fourtenight。

items.en: It settled as fortnight in spelling.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 fortnight。

items.en: British English kept it as the normal word for two weeks.
items.cn: 英式英语把它保留为两星期的常用词。

items.en: It also came to name a two-week holiday.
items.cn: 它也开始表示两周假期。

note.en: Fortnight is compared with similar-looking words and with words for time periods.
note.cn: 把 fortnight 与形近词以及表示时段的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: fortnight 是十四个夜晚捆成的一个词。

normal.en: We will meet in a fortnight.

normal.en: The club meets every fortnight.

normal.en: The letter arrived a fortnight ago.

abstract.en: A fortnight is two weeks holding hands.

abstract.en: British speech folds nights into time.

abstract.en: Fourteen days can change a whole life.
abstract.cn: 十四天可以改变一生。

root: 由古英语 feowertyne niht（十四个夜晚）缩合而成，核心义「十四天」。

sensesIntro.en: Fortnight means two weeks, a two-week interval, or a two-week holiday.
sensesIntro.cn: fortnight 意为两星期、每两周或两周假期。

core.en: Fourteen nights joined into one block of time.
core.cn: 十四个夜晚连成的一整块时间。

branches.en: Fourteen days pass as one unit.
branches.cn: 十四天作为一个单位过去。

branches.en: The unit returns on a schedule.
branches.cn: 这个时间单位按计划重复。

branches.en: The unit becomes a holiday.
branches.cn: 这个时间单位变成一段假期。

branches.en: Two weeks can be time or freedom.
branches.cn: 两周既可以是时间，也可以是自由。

branches.en: A length and a rhythm share one word.
branches.cn: 一段时间与一种节奏共用一个词。

intro.en: Fortnight builds a small family of two-week and night words.
intro.cn: fortnight 构成表示两周与夜晚的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Fortnight is Germanic; Latin duae hebdomades, two weeks, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fortnight 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 duae hebdomades（两周）只是语义对应词。

definition_zh: 要塞；堡垒；设防城市；坚固屏障（比喻）
definition_en: a heavily fortified place built to resist attack, or something regarded as an unbreakable defence
core_image: 厚墙上只开一道窄门，门前是斜坡与壕沟，墙顶的守军能看见来路每一寸
scene: 山路在壕沟前突然收窄，只剩一道窄门可以进去。The fortress held out for a year while the valley below changed hands twice.
sceneCN: 这里 fortress 指「为抵御进攻而设防的要塞」（第 1 个义项：堡垒、要塞）；句意为这座要塞坚守了一年，其间下方山谷两度易手。图中可辨识物件：厚墙、窄门、壕沟、斜坡。

pos.zh: 要塞；堡垒；巩固的防御据点

senses.title: A fortified stronghold
senses.definition: a large fortified place with thick walls, ditches and defensive works
senses.definitionCN: 拥有厚墙、壕沟与防御工事的大型设防之地
senses.example: The fortress commands the only road through the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这座要塞控制着穿越山口的唯一道路。
senses.why: the word comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'strong', so a fortress is simply a place made strong against attack.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「坚固」的拉丁形容词，因此要塞就是一个被造得能抗攻击的地方。

senses.title: A walled town
senses.definition: a town whose whole perimeter is enclosed by walls and gates
senses.definitionCN: 整个周边被城墙与城门围住的城镇
senses.example: The old fortress is still inhabited inside its ring of walls.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧设防城镇仍有人住在城墙围成的圈内。
senses.why: when a whole settlement is fortified, the word names the town as much as the walls.
senses.whyCN: 当整个聚落都被设防时，这个词指城镇本身，也指那些墙。

senses.title: A system of permanent works
senses.definition: the whole set of bastions, ramparts and batteries built to hold a position
senses.definitionCN: 为守住阵地而建的棱堡、壁垒与炮台的整体
senses.example: Engineers surveyed the fortress before adding two new bastions.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师勘测了整片工事，之后加建两座棱堡。
senses.why: military usage treats the fortress as a system, not a single building.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法把要塞视作一个系统，而非单栋建筑。

senses.title: An unbreakable barrier
senses.definition: something treated as impossible to penetrate or overcome
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法穿透或攻克的事物
senses.example: The company built a fortress of patents around its core product.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司围绕核心产品建起一座专利堡垒。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only resistance: a fortress does not need walls to be a fortress.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留「抵抗」：一座堡垒不必有墙也能是堡垒。

senses.title: A forward military base
senses.definition: a strongly held position at the edge of controlled territory
senses.definitionCN: 位于控制区边缘、被强力据守的阵地
senses.example: The brigade turned the village into a fortress on the front line.
senses.exampleCN: 该旅把这座村庄变成前线上的一座堡垒。
senses.why: modern armies reuse the word for any position they intend to hold rather than pass through.
senses.whyCN: 现代军队把这个词用于任何打算守住而非路过的阵地。

senses.title: The inner keep of a castle
senses.definition: the strongest inner part of a castle, the last place of resistance
senses.definitionCN: 城堡中最坚固的内部，是最后抵抗之处
senses.example: The outer walls fell, but the fortress in the centre held.
senses.exampleCN: 外墙陷落，但中央的核心堡垒仍在坚守。
senses.why: a castle can contain a fortress: the word marks the part designed never to fall.
senses.whyCN: 城堡之内可以有一座要塞：这个词标记的是那部分永不打算陷落的结构。

senses.title: An unyielding position
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：寸步不让的立场
senses.definition: a political or personal stance maintained against all pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在各种压力下都不退让的政治或个人立场
senses.example: The ministry became a fortress of resistance to the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门成了抵抗这项改革的堡垒。
senses.why: people defend institutions as they defend walls, so the word describes stubbornness as well as stone.
senses.whyCN: 人捍卫机构如同捍卫城墙，因此这个词既描述石头，也描述固执。

senses.title: A fortress-like structure
senses.definition: a modern building whose massing and small openings make it look defensive
senses.definitionCN: 体量厚重、开窗狭小、看上去带防御性的现代建筑
senses.example: The new museum is a fortress of concrete with almost no windows.
senses.exampleCN: 新博物馆是一座几乎没有窗的混凝土堡垒。
senses.why: architects borrow the word when a building's form, not its function, suggests defence.
senses.whyCN: 当建筑的形式而非功能暗示防御时，建筑师便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Fortress comes from a Latin adjective for 'strong' through medieval and Old French forms meaning 'a strong place'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fortress 来自一个意为「坚固」的拉丁形容词，经中世纪拉丁语与古法语中表示「坚固之地」的形式而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, mighty or brave, and it described both bodies and buildings.
items.cn: fortis 意为坚固的、强大的或勇敢的，既能描述身体也能描述建筑。

items.en: Medieval Latin fortalitia named a strong place, formed from the adjective with a suffix for a built thing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 fortalitia 指坚固之地，由该形容词加表示建筑物的后缀构成。

items.en: Old French forteresse carried the word into English, where it first meant a fortified town or castle.
items.cn: 古法语 forteresse 把这个词带入英语，最初指设防城镇或城堡。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was used for the new low, thick, angular works designed to resist cannon.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词用于指为抵御火炮而设计的新式低厚棱角工事。

items.en: In the twentieth century fortress spread to politics and business, as in fortress Europe or a fortress of patents.
items.cn: 二十世纪，fortress 扩展到政治与商业，如「壁垒欧洲」或「专利堡垒」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of fortis is not settled, and the Indo-European root commonly proposed for it is a reconstruction only.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：fortis 在拉丁语之前的谱系尚无定论，通常为其提出的印欧语词根只是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same strength or fortification stock; group two holds defensive places and buildings.
note.cn: 第一组同出「坚固」或「筑城」词干的词；第二组是其他防御性地点与建筑。

entries.definition: To strengthen a place against attack; the verb acts on a site, while the noun names the site itself.
entries.definitionCN: 加固某地以御攻击；动词作用于地点，名词则指该地点本身。

entries.definition: Courage in pain or adversity; it shares the strength root but names a personal quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在痛苦或逆境中的坚毅；同出「坚固」词根，但指个人品质。

entries.definition: The walls and works built to defend a place, or the act of building them.
entries.definitionCN: 为防卫某地而建的墙与工事，或建造行为。

entries.definition: A person's strong point; from the same Latin adjective but used in a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 某人的长处；同出拉丁形容词，但用于不同意义。

entries.definition: A fortified home of a lord; it is both house and stronghold, while a fortress is primarily military.
entries.definitionCN: 领主的设防居所，既是住宅也是据点；而 fortress 主要是军事性的。

entries.definition: The strongest part of a city's defences, often on high ground; it is a fortress inside a town.
entries.definitionCN: 城市防御中最坚固的部分，常位于高地；是城镇内部的要塞。

entries.definition: A place firmly held against opposition; it can be a fortress or a political base.
entries.definitionCN: 被牢牢守住的据点，可以是军事要塞或政治基地。

entries.definition: A projecting part of a fortification; it is one piece of a fortress, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 防御工事中向外突出的部分，是要塞的一件构件而非整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real strength root, the real siege terms and the real modern metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「坚固」词根、真实的攻城术语与真实的现代比喻。

normal.en: The root means strong, so a fortress is a place made artificially strong.
normal.cn: 词根意为坚固，因此要塞就是一处被人为加固的地方。

normal.en: The family runs fortress, fortify, fortification, fortified, fortitude, fortalice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fortress、fortify、fortification、fortified、fortitude、fortalice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: mountain fortress, fortress town, fortress Europe.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：山地要塞、设防城镇、壁垒欧洲。

normal.en: A castle is a home that can fight; a fortress is a fighter that can house troops.
normal.cn: 城堡是能作战的家，要塞是能驻军的战士。

normal.en: The modern metaphor keeps only one feature: you cannot get through.
normal.cn: 现代比喻只保留一个特征：你过不去。

abstract.en: Picture a door so narrow that an army must enter one person at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一道窄到军队只能一人一人进入的门。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with no windows, only arrow slits like thin closed eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一面没有窗的墙，只有像细闭合眼睛的箭孔。

abstract.en: Picture a company that answers every question with a patent number.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司对每个问题都回以一个专利号。

examples.en: The fortress surrendered only after its water cistern was breached.
examples.cn: 这座要塞直到蓄水池被攻破后才投降。

examples.en: The border has become a fortress of fences and cameras.
examples.cn: 边境已成了一道由围栏与摄像头构成的壁垒。

examples.en: Its old fortress walls now hold a public garden.
examples.cn: 它旧日的要塞城墙如今围着一座公共花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: fort（坚固）+ ress（场所）→ 被造得坚固的地方 → 要塞、堡垒

root: 古法语 forteresse 来自中世纪拉丁 fortalitia「坚固之地」，其基础是拉丁 fortis「坚固的、强大的」；英语 fortress。fortis 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，相关印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one refusal: a place refuses entry, and that refusal scales from walls to towns, works, bases, keeps, beliefs, institutions and finally to a building's shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种拒绝展开：某处拒绝进入；这种拒绝从城墙扩展到城镇、工事群、据点、核心、信念、机构，最后扩展到建筑的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick stone and one narrow gate, with every approach visible from the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚石与一道窄门，从墙上能看见每一条来路。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a stronghold and a walled town are the same refusal at two scales.
branches.cn: 地点：据点与设防城镇，是同一拒绝的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: permanent works and forward bases turn the single wall into a military machine.
branches.cn: 系统：永备工事与前沿据点把单面墙变成一台军事机器。

branches.en: THE BARRIER: patents and institutions become fortresses when they refuse to be crossed.
branches.cn: 屏障：专利与机构在拒绝被越过时就成为堡垒。

branches.en: THE LAST CORE: the keep is the part built on the assumption that everything else may fall.
branches.cn: 最后的核：核心堡垒是按「其余皆可能陷落」的假设造出的那一部分。

branches.en: THE LOOK: a modern concrete mass borrows defence as a style.
branches.cn: 外观：现代混凝土体量把防御当作一种风格借用过来。

intro.en: Fortress is a Latin strength adjective plus a suffix for a built place, and the same stem supplies the whole fortification family.
intro.cn: fortress 是一个拉丁语「坚固」形容词加表示建筑物的后缀，同一词干给出了整族筑城词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis and the medieval noun fortalitia passed through Old French; English then built fortify, fortification and fortitude on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 与中世纪名词 fortalitia 经古法语传来；英语随后用同一词干构成 fortify、fortification 与 fortitude。

items.example: Fortis described walls and soldiers alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既能描述墙，也能描述士兵。

items.example: Fortalitia named the place, not the quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指地点，而非性质。

items.example: The forteresse guarded the river crossing.
items.exampleCN: 这座要塞守卫着河流渡口。

items.example: They fortified the gate with earth.

items.meaning: defensive works or the building of them
items.example: The fortification followed the hill's contour.
items.exampleCN: 防御工事顺着山势延展。

items.example: A fortified village blocked the road.
items.exampleCN: 一座设防村庄堵住了道路。

items.example: She bore the siege with fortitude.

definition_en: toward the front, a player near the front, or moving toward the future
core_image: 一个箭头朝前指着，队伍顺着箭头方向移动
scene: 队伍慢慢向前移动。The line moved forward slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 forward 是「向前」（第 1 个义项）；句意：队伍慢慢向前移动。

senses.title: Toward the front
senses.definition: in the direction of the front
senses.definitionCN: 朝着前方的方向
senses.example: The line moved forward slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍慢慢向前移动。
senses.why: This is the basic direction sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的方向义项。

senses.title: A front player
senses.definition: a player whose main job is to attack
senses.definitionCN: 主要任务是进攻的球员
senses.example: The forward scored the winning goal.
senses.exampleCN: 前锋打进了制胜球。
senses.why: The front of the team takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 球队的前部得到这个名称。

senses.title: Toward the future
senses.definition: moving toward what is ahead in time
senses.definitionCN: 朝着时间上更靠前的方向
senses.example: We look forward to the new term.
senses.exampleCN: 我们期待新学期。
senses.why: Space ahead becomes time ahead.
senses.whyCN: 前方的空间变成了未来的时间。

intro.en: Forward is an old compound of fore and ward.
intro.cn: forward 是由 fore 和 ward 构成的古老复合词。

items.en: Foreweard meant toward the front.
items.cn: foreweard 意为朝向前方。

items.en: The form became forward.
items.cn: 词形演变为 forward。

items.en: The adverb named movement ahead.
items.cn: 副词义表示向前的移动。

items.en: Sports gave it the sense of a front player.
items.cn: 体育赋予它前锋的含义。

items.en: The phrase look forward to meant to expect.
items.cn: 短语 look forward to 意为期待。

note.en: Forward is compared with similar-looking words and with direction words.
note.cn: 把 forward 与形近词以及方向词作比较。

definition_en: the preserved remains or trace of an animal or plant from a past geological age, or something outdated
core_image: 页岩被劈开，一片鱼形的黑色印痕露出来，鳞片排列仍看得清
scene: 页岩劈开时，一片鱼形的黑色印痕露出来，鳞片排列还看得清。 The split shale revealed a fish fossil with scales still legible.
sceneCN: 这里 fossil 指「保存在岩层中的古生物遗体」（第 1 个义项：地质时期生物的保存遗体或印痕）；句意为劈开的页岩中露出一具鱼化石，鳞片仍清晰可辨。图中可辨识物件：劈开的页岩、鱼形印痕、鳞片纹理、地质锤。

pos.zh: 化石；化石标本；（口语）老顽固、过时的人或物
化石的；从化石中得来的（如 fossil fuel）

senses.title: Preserved remains in rock
senses.titleCN: 保存在岩层中的古生物遗体
senses.definition: the remains, impression or cast of an organism preserved in rock from an earlier geological period
senses.definitionCN: 保存在较早地质时期岩层中的生物遗体、印痕或铸型
senses.example: The museum's oldest fossil is a fern print from the Carboniferous.
senses.exampleCN: 馆藏最古老的化石是一件石炭纪的蕨类印痕。
senses.why: the Latin word meant 'dug up', so any organic trace hard enough to survive in stone qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词义为「挖出来的」，因此任何硬到能在石中留存的生物痕迹都算。

senses.title: A specimen in a collection
senses.definition: one catalogued piece held in a museum or study collection, with a number and a locality
senses.definitionCN: 博物馆或研究收藏中编了号、记了产地的一件标本
senses.example: Each fossil in the drawer carries a label with its grid reference.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里每件化石都带着写有网格坐标的标签。
senses.why: collecting practice turns the mass noun into a countable object, so a fossil can be borrowed, cast and photographed.
senses.whyCN: 收藏实践把不可数的总称变成可数物件，于是化石可以出借、翻模与拍摄。

senses.title: A species that has barely changed
senses.titleCN: 存活至今而形态几乎未变的物种
senses.definition: a living species that closely resembles its ancient relatives and has changed very little
senses.definitionCN: 与远古亲属极为相似、变化极小的现存物种
senses.example: The ginkgo is often called a living fossil, though its genes have moved on.
senses.exampleCN: 银杏常被称为活化石，尽管其基因已经变化。
senses.why: the phrase is a deliberate paradox: the organism is alive, yet read as if it were stone.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是刻意的悖论：生物还活着，却像石头一样被解读。

senses.title: Fuel from ancient organic matter
senses.titleCN: 源自远古有机质的燃料
senses.definition: coal, oil or gas formed from buried organisms and burned as fuel, used attributively
senses.definitionCN: 由埋藏的远古生物形成、被燃烧作燃料的煤、石油或天然气，作定语使用
senses.example: The city pledged to cut fossil fuel use by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 该市承诺把化石燃料用量削减三分之一。
senses.why: the attributive use compresses a long history: the fuel is ancient sunlight stored in rock.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法压缩了一段长历史：这种燃料是储在岩石里的远古阳光。

senses.title: A person stuck in the past
senses.titleCN: 口语：思想陈旧的老顽固
senses.definition: a person with fixed, old-fashioned views who resists any change
senses.definitionCN: 观念固定、守旧、抗拒任何改变的人
senses.example: The committee's chairman is an old fossil who still uses a typewriter.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会主席是个还在用打字机的老顽固。
senses.why: the insult works because a fossil is something that stopped changing long ago and now merely persists.
senses.whyCN: 这个贬称之所以有效，是因为化石早已停止变化，只是仍留在那里。

senses.title: An outdated institution or idea
senses.definition: a rule, practice or idea that survives long after its conditions have gone
senses.definitionCN: 在原有条件消失后仍存留很久的规则、做法或观念
senses.example: The licensing rule is a fossil of the cartage era.
senses.exampleCN: 这项许可规定是马车运输时代留下的化石。
senses.why: institutions leave traces the way organisms do, so the metaphor transfers without much strain.
senses.whyCN: 制度像生物一样留下痕迹，因此这个比喻转移过来并不费力。

senses.title: A trace fossil
senses.titleCN: 遗迹化石（活动留下的痕迹）
senses.definition: a preserved record of an organism's activity, such as a track, burrow or feeding mark, rather than its body
senses.definitionCN: 生物活动而非遗体留下的保存记录，如足迹、潜穴或觅食痕
senses.example: The sandstone holds trace fossils but no bones at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这层砂岩只有遗迹化石，完全没有骨骼。
senses.why: palaeontology separates the body from the behaviour, and the compound keeps that distinction visible.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学把遗体与行为分开，这个复合词让这一区分保持可见。

senses.title: A fossil used for dating
senses.definition: a species whose known time range lets a rock layer be assigned an age
senses.definitionCN: 已知生存时限可用于给岩层定年的物种
senses.example: A single ammonite fossil fixed the bed to the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 一件菊石化石把这层定为侏罗纪。
senses.why: biostratigraphy treats certain fossils as index markers, valued for their date rather than their beauty.
senses.whyCN: 生物地层学把某些化石当作标志物，看重的是年代而非美观。

senses.title: Anything preserved in stone
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：被保存在石头里的
senses.definition: preserved in rock, or made of the mineral matter that replaced an organism
senses.definitionCN: 保存在岩石中的，或由替换生物体的矿物质构成的
senses.example: The fossil wood still shows annual growth rings.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石木仍能看到年轮。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the oldest literal sense, describing the state of preservation rather than a category of object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留最古老的字面义，描写保存状态，而非物类。

intro.en: Fossil comes from Latin fossilis 'dug up', from fodere 'to dig'. English adopted it in the seventeenth century for anything dug from the earth, before it narrowed to organic remains. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fossil 来自拉丁 fossilis「挖出来的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」。英语于十七世纪引入，最初泛指从地下挖出之物，后来收窄为生物遗体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fodere meant 'to dig', and its participle fossus produced fossilis 'dug up, dug out'.
items.cn: fodere 意为「挖掘」，其分词 fossus 产生 fossilis「被挖出的」。

items.en: In sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Latin, fossilis covered minerals, gems and anything else dug from the ground, not only living things.
items.cn: 在十六、十七世纪的拉丁语中，fossilis 涵盖矿物、宝石以及一切从地下挖出之物，并不限于生物。

items.en: English naturalists gradually restricted fossil to the remains and traces of once-living things found in rock.
items.cn: 英国博物学者逐渐把 fossil 收窄为岩石中发现的、曾属生物的那些遗体与痕迹。

items.en: The nineteenth century added fossil fuel, and the same period produced the joking use for an out-of-date person.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添了 fossil fuel 一义，同一时期也产生了戏指过时之人的用法。

items.en: The phrase living fossil was applied to species that seem unchanged since deep time, an image rather than a taxonomic category.
items.cn: living fossil 一语用于自远古以来似无变化的物种，是意象而非分类学范畴。

items.en: Source uncertain (only the first dating is in doubt): the Latin derivation is secure, but the exact decade of the English narrowing varies by author.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：拉丁派生是确定的，但英语收窄的确切年代因作者而异。

note.en: Group one separates fossil from words built on the same Latin dig-family and from look-alikes; group two separates it from other remains and from the figurative senses.
note.cn: 第一组把 fossil 与同出拉丁「挖」族的词及形近词分开；第二组区分它与其它遗体说法及比喻义。

entries.definition: To make or become a fossil; the noun names the object, the verb the process.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为化石或变成化石；名词指对象，动词指过程。

entries.definition: Fossil plus -ferous 'bearing': rock that contains fossils, said of a layer.
entries.definitionCN: fossil 加 -ferous「承载」：含化石的，用于形容岩层。

entries.definition: From Latin fossa 'a ditch', also from fodere; it means a trench, not a remain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fossa「沟」，亦出 fodere；意为壕沟，而非遗体。

entries.definition: An Australian English verb for prospecting among old workings; its origin is uncertain and not the Latin fossilis line.
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚英语动词，指在旧矿渣中搜寻；来源不确定，不属拉丁 fossilis 一线。

entries.definition: Something that survives from an earlier time, including objects and customs; it need not be mineralised.
entries.definitionCN: 从较早时期留存之物，包括器物与习俗；不必矿化。

entries.definition: What is left of a body, recent or ancient; fossil adds deep time and preservation in rock.
entries.definitionCN: 遗体残留，不论新旧；fossil 增添深时间与岩中保存之意。

entries.definition: A replica formed when minerals fill a mould left by a dissolved organism; one kind of fossil.
entries.definitionCN: 矿物填充生物溶解后留下的模腔所形成的复制体，是化石的一种。

entries.definition: A body preserved by drying or cold rather than mineralisation; it is not usually called a fossil.
entries.definitionCN: 靠干燥或寒冷而非矿化保存的尸体，通常不称化石。

normal.en: Latin fossilis 'dug up' from fodere 'to dig': what the hammer brings out of the rock.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fossilis「挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖」：锤子从岩中取出的东西。

normal.en: The family runs fossil, fossils, fossilize, fossilization, fossiliferous, subfossil.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fossil、fossils、fossilize、fossilization、fossiliferous、subfossil。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fossil record, fossil fuel, trace fossil, living fossil.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：化石记录、化石燃料、遗迹化石、活化石。

normal.en: The same Latin dig-root gives fosse 'ditch', a hole rather than a remain.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁「挖」根还给出 fosse「壕沟」，是洞而非遗体。

normal.en: The insult is geological: something that stopped changing long ago and merely persists.
normal.cn: 这个贬称是地质式的：早已停止变化，只是仍留在那里。

branches.en: PRESERVED FORM: the noun and the adjective describe the same mineral state.
branches.cn: 保存的形态：名词与形容词描写同一种矿物状态。

branches.en: OBJECT AND TOOL: one fossil is a specimen, another is a date.
branches.cn: 对象与工具：一件是标本，另一件是年代。

branches.en: TRACES OF LIFE: a living species and a burrow both count as traces of the ancient.

branches.en: STORED SUNLIGHT: fuel is the same burial read as energy.

branches.en: FROZEN THINGS: a person and a rule both stopped changing and merely persist.

items.exampleCN: 他们创办了这家慈善机构。

items.example: The town was founded long ago.
